name: Workit Health
one_liner: App-based treatment for opioid and alcohol use: video visits for Suboxone or naltrexone, plus counseling, in about 14 states.
best_for: Adults with opioid use disorder who want buprenorphine (Suboxone) by video
Adults who want naltrexone or acamprosate for drinking
People with commercial insurance, or Medicaid in a state where Workit takes it
People in rural areas far from a clinic
not_for: Anyone in crisis or overdose: call 911, or call or text 988
People who need medically supervised detox or residential treatment
People with Texas or Florida Medicaid (not accepted)
short_description: Telehealth medication (Suboxone, naltrexone) and counseling for opioid and alcohol use through an app; insurance, some Medicaid, or self-pay.
long_description: Workit Health is a US telehealth addiction treatment provider. Through its app you have video visits with clinicians who can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone) for opioid use disorder or naltrexone or acamprosate for alcohol use disorder, plus counseling, groups and self-paced lessons. A 2026 review listed 14 states: Arizona, California, Florida, Illinois, Michigan, Montana, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas and Washington. It accepts many Aetna, Cigna, Blue Cross Blue Shield, UnitedHealthcare and Humana plans, and Medicaid and Medicare in some states (not Medicaid in Texas or Florida); its state pages say most insured members pay $25–$35 a month. Self-pay was reported at $90 for the first visit then $75 a week for opioid care, and $250 then $150 a month for alcohol care. Workit researchers have published retrospective studies of its patients, including one of 1,816 rural patients in which 62% were still in care at three months. Its privacy policy says it may run ad pixels on its website.

pricing.starting_price: Copay with insurance (most pay $25–$35/month); $75/week self-pay for opioid care
pricing.notes: Self-pay reported as $90 first appointment then $75/week for opioid treatment, $250 first month then $150/month for alcohol treatment (2026 review); Workit's own FAQ quotes about $300/month. Medication is billed separately by the pharmacy. Medicaid and Medicare in select states; Medicaid not accepted in Texas or Florida.

privacy.notes: Policy (updated Dec 2025) says it may run ad pixels through Google Tag Manager on its website; clinic records are covered by its HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 notice. A 2023 Senate letter and class action raised ad-pixel concerns (allegations, not regulator findings).

seo.title: Workit Health: Review & Pricing | HeyPsych
seo.meta_description: Workit Health provides online addiction treatment for alcohol and opioid use disorders with medication, therapy, and coaching covered by most insurance.

faqs.a: Yes, Workit accepts many major insurance plans and Medicaid in several states. Contact them to verify your specific coverage. Insurance typically covers medication management visits and therapy components.

For opioid use disorder, Workit prescribes buprenorphine (Suboxone). For alcohol use disorder, medications like naltrexone or other FDA-approved options may be used. Medication is combined with therapy and coaching for comprehensive treatment.

faqs.q: How does the Workit app work?
faqs.a: The Workit app provides CBT-based therapeutic exercises, video sessions with counselors, group support meetings, and peer coaching. You can engage with content between appointments on your own schedule. It's designed for flexibility around work and life.

faqs.q: Is Workit effective for addiction treatment?
faqs.a: Workit uses evidence-based approaches: FDA-approved medications combined with behavioral therapy. Published outcomes show significant reductions in substance use among participants. The combination of medication and therapy is supported by strong clinical evidence.

clinical_trials.study: Retention of rural Workit Health patients in telehealth buprenorphine treatment

citation.authors: Lira MC, Jimes C, Coffey MJ
citation.title: Retention in Telehealth Treatment for Opioid Use Disorder Among Rural Populations: A Retrospective Cohort Study

clinical_trials.outcome: 75%, 62% and 52% retained at 1, 3 and 6 months across 14 states; no control group; authors employed by Workit.

clinical_trials.study: Home delivery vs pharmacy pickup of buprenorphine among Workit Health patients in Texas

citation.authors: Lira MC, Hendy LE, Liakas A, et al.
citation.title: Early findings on home delivery of buprenorphine and retention in treatment for opioid use disorder

clinical_trials.outcome: Three-month retention 82.6% with home delivery vs 58.9% with pharmacy pickup; non-randomized, small, company-authored.

primary_uses: Buprenorphine (Suboxone) treatment for opioid use disorder by video
Naltrexone or acamprosate for alcohol use disorder
Self-paced recovery lessons in the app

availability.note: About 14 states (AZ, CA, FL, IL, MI, MT, NJ, NM, NY, NC, OH, OK, TX, WA per a 2026 review); Medicaid only in some of them.

patient_summary: You sign up in the Workit app, check your insurance, and meet a clinician by video who can prescribe buprenorphine (Suboxone) for opioids or naltrexone for alcohol, with counseling and lessons in the app. Most insured members pay about $25–$35 a month; self-pay is roughly $75 a week for opioid care. Medication is billed separately by your pharmacy.
